newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia to probe telecommunications billing.
newsitem.headline: Australia to probe telecommunications billing.

text.p: The Australian government on Monday announced an independent investigation into the billing practices of Telstra Corp and other service providers.
Communications Minister Richard Alston said in a statement consultancies consultancies International Consulting Services and CommStrategies International will conduct the investigation.

They will talk to state telecoms giant Telstra Corp, AAPT Pty Ltd , Primus Axicorp, Corptel, and Switch in order to assess the impact of billing problems on customers, and the steps required to resolve any shortcomings.
The inquiry, due to report on October 27, will investigate the quality of services and approaches to resolving problems of Telstra and other carriers.
"In doing this the consultancies will compare current billing processes and service levels with those in the United Kingdom and United States," Alston said.
"This is designed to ensure that the government's aim of global best practice is achieved."
He said the investigation should would also help in drafting a code of practice and ensuring competition in the newly deregulated market.
Problems with billing have created disputes between Telstra and its customers and between Telstra and other service providers.
The government last week announced plans to remove limits to foreign ownership of telecommunications companies and also plans to soon float a third of Telstra.
Australia's telecoms industry was deregulated from July 1, sparking increased competition and prompting the entry of several new carriers.
